content.text: Motion is one of the most fundamental concepts in physics. Everything around us is in motion — from the electrons orbiting atomic nuclei to planets orbiting stars. To describe motion precisely, physicists use quantities such as speed, velocity, and acceleration. While these terms are often used interchangeably in everyday language, they have very specific and distinct meanings in physics.

In this lesson, we will carefully define distance, displacement, speed, velocity, and acceleration. We will then develop the equations of motion (often called the SUVAT equations) that allow us to solve a wide range of problems involving objects moving with constant acceleration. Mastering these concepts and equations is essential for understanding mechanics and many other areas of physics.

The following two SUVAT equations go beyond the core IGCSE syllabus. They are included for enrichment and are not required for your exam. The key equations you need are $v = u + at$ and $s = \frac{(u + v)}{2} \times t$.
This gives the displacement in terms of initial velocity, acceleration, and time. It can be derived by considering that the average velocity is
s = \frac{u + (u + at)}{2} \times t = \frac{2u + at}{2} \times t = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2
This equation is useful when time is not known or not required. It relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement.
This simply states that displacement equals average velocity multiplied by time, which is valid when acceleration is constant.

"Speed and velocity are the same thing."
Speed is a scalar (magnitude only); velocity is a vector (magnitude and direction). A car turning a corner at constant speed has a changing velocity because its direction changes.
"An object that is slowing down has negative velocity."

Not necessarily. An object moving in the positive direction but slowing down has positive velocity and negative acceleration. The sign of velocity tells you the direction of motion, not whether the object is speeding up or slowing down.
Acceleration means the velocity is changing. This could mean speeding up, slowing down, or changing direction. Deceleration is a special case where the object is losing speed.
"If acceleration is zero, the object is not moving."
Zero acceleration means the velocity is not changing. The object could be stationary or moving at constant velocity. An object cruising at 30 m/s on a motorway has zero acceleration.
